title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your day — what you usually do and what you're doing right now — using the present habitual and present continuous.
intro:
This is the unit where Sindhi verbs come alive. Sindhi makes its everyday present tense by adding a small helper — **ٿو** (tho) — to a verb form with a personal ending: **مان وڃان ٿو** 'I go'. For 'I am going (right now)', it uses **پيو** (peyo): **مان پيو وڃان**.

All Sindhi infinitives end in **-ṇu** (ڻ): ڪرڻ karaṇu, وڃڻ vañaṇu, اٿڻ uthaṇu. Drop the -aṇu and you have the stem: ڪر-, وڃ-, اٿ-.

vocab.note: هٿ منهن ڌوئڻ = to wash up (lit. wash hands and face).
Irregular past ويو vayo. Note the ñ (ڃ).
Past ڪيو kayo. 3pl present: ڪن ٿا.
m. ڪم ڪرڻ = to work; ڪم تي = at work.
f. نماز پڙهڻ = to pray (lit. read prayer).

vocab.en: to walk; to go; to work (of machines)
vocab.note: هلو! = let's go! بتي هلي وئي = the power went.
ٿو (m sg), ٿي (f sg), ٿا (m pl / polite), ٿيون (f pl).
پيو (m sg), پئي (f sg), پيا (m pl), پيون (f pl).

grammar.title: The present tense: verb + ٿو
grammar.body:
The Sindhi present (for habits, facts and general statements) has two parts: the **verb stem + a personal ending**, then the helper **ٿو / ٿي / ٿا / ٿيون** agreeing in gender and number. Here is وڃڻ 'to go' (stem وڃ vañ-):

مان وڃان ٿو / ٿي — vañāṃ tho / thī — I go
تون وڃين ٿو / ٿي — vañeṃ tho / vañīṃ thī — you (intimate) go
هو وڃي ٿو / هوءَ وڃي ٿي — vañe tho / thī — he / she goes
اسين وڃون ٿا / ٿيون — vañūṃ thā / thyūṃ — we go
توهان وڃو ٿا / ٿيون — vaño thā / thyūṃ — you (polite) go
هو وڃن ٿا / ٿيون — vañan thā / thyūṃ — they go

Stems ending in a vowel add -y-: ڪرڻ → ڪريان ٿو karyāṃ tho, ڳالهائڻ → ڳالهايان ٿو. One irregular to note: ڪرڻ 'to do' has 3pl **ڪن ٿا** (kan thā).

**Negative**: نه + ٿو is written as one word **نٿو / نٿي / نٿا**, usually placed *before* the verb: مان نٿو وڃان 'I don't go'.

In relaxed speech the helper often comes first: **مان ٿو وڃان** — same meaning.

grammar.title: Right now: پيو + verb (present continuous)
grammar.body:
For an action **in progress right now**, Sindhi uses **پيو** (peyo) — literally 'fallen (into)' — before the same verb form, *without* ٿو. پيو agrees like an adjective:

پيو peyo (m sg) · پئي paī (f sg) · پيا pyā (m pl) · پيون pyūṃ (f pl)

مان پيو لکان — I am writing (man)
هوءَ پئي پچائي — she is cooking
ٻار پيا کيڏن — the children are playing

You will also hear an Urdu-style continuous with **رهيو آهي** (rahyo āhe): هو ماني کائي رهيو آهي 'he is eating'. Both are correct; the پيو form is more distinctively Sindhi and very common in speech.

Use ٿو for habits (روز 'every day', هميشه 'always', ڪڏهن ڪڏهن 'sometimes') and پيو for 'right now' (هاڻي 'now').

culture: The day in much of Sindh starts early, with the dawn prayer (فجر) for observant Muslims, and is organised around the heat: in summer, shops and offices may slow down in the afternoon and life moves outdoors in the evening, when people sit in courtyards and on rooftops, visit relatives and stroll in markets. In villages, the day follows the farming calendar — wheat (ڪڻڪ) in winter, rice and cotton in summer — and the hours of irrigation water from the canals of the Indus.

lessons.title: Getting up and getting ready

tip.title: The present: verb + ٿو
tip.body:
- Habits and facts: verb stem + a personal ending, then **ٿو / ٿي / ٿا**: مان اٿان ٿو · تون اٿين ٿو · هو اٿي ٿو · اسين اٿون ٿا · توهان اٿو ٿا · هو اٿن ٿا.
- **ٿو** for a man, **ٿي** for a woman, **ٿا** for plural or polite.
- 'Don't': **نٿو / نٿي** before the verb: مان نٿو اٿان.

tip.title: Go, come, do
tip.body:
- **وڃڻ** go: مان وڃان ٿو, هو وڃي ٿو, اسين وڃون ٿا, توهان وڃو ٿا, هو وڃن ٿا.
- **ڪرڻ** do: مان ڪريان ٿو, توهان ڪريو ٿا — but 'they do' is **ڪن ٿا**.
- 'To' a place usually needs no word: گهر وڃان ٿو 'I go home', آفيس وڃان ٿي.

lessons.title: What are you doing right now?

tip.title: Right now: پيو + verb
tip.body:
- For something happening **right now**, put **پيو** before the verb and drop ٿو: مان چانهه پيو پيئان.
- پيو agrees: **پيو** (m) · **پئي** (f) · **پيا** (m pl, polite) · **پيون** (f pl).
- ٿو = habit (روز, هميشه); پيو = now (هاڻي).

lessons.title: Always, often, never

tip.title: Habit or right now?
tip.body:
- Habits go with **ٿو**: **هميشه** always, **اڪثر** often, **عام طور تي** usually, **ڪڏهن ڪڏهن** sometimes.
- 'Never' = **ڪڏهن به** + **نٿو / نٿي**: مان ڪڏهن به دير نٿو ڪريان.
- Right now goes with **پيو**: هاڻي ڪتاب پيو پڙهي.
